analysis: The PR changes only two Markdown files, docs/architecture/inference.md and docs/developer/serving-performance-qualification.md. It contains no executable code, configuration, wire-format or key-handling change. I read the supplied head text of inference.md (lines 1235-1821) and the patch for serving-performance-qualification.md. The hunks in inference.md at head lines 632-638 and 882-918 were visible only as patch excerpts, and the second is truncated. Those two hunks describe three admission-estimator corrections: per-step decode charging, out-of-order observation freshness anchoring, and a rollback switch, DARKBLOOM_TTFT_ADMISSION_FIXES=0. The corrections affect deadline and TTFT admission, which concern availability and scheduling. The documentation says physical admission, actual deadline expiry, queue/cache projection and the GlobalKVCacheBudget gates still apply. I found no claim that weakens attestation, E2E encryption, App Attest authorization, the TB-002 coordinator-to-provider boundary or the T-041 prefix-cache posture (SSD TTL, HMAC lookup tags, coordinator-authored cacheSalt). The supplied text keeps the existing statements: the cache sits outside the sampler identity, media stays noncacheable, and nothing is written to disk for in-memory video assets (T-050). The doc states that catalog, hosted-serving and performance qualification are not granted by availability or by documentation, consistent with the scope rules. Remaining questions for later passes: whether the described estimator code in AdmissionRateEstimators.swift and EnginePerformanceMeasurements matches the documentation, and whether the new per-step decode charging could under-price admission under load. That code is not in this batch, so it is an unverified contract and not a finding.
